draft.title: A significant Buddhist practice
card: A Buddhist practice is something Buddhists do that puts their beliefs into action. It lets them show and strengthen what they hold to be true.
Temple puja
acts of respect and offering, such as bowing, chanting and offering flowers, candles and incense before an image of the Buddha. Flowers that wilt remind Buddhists that all things are impermanent.
Wesak
a festival, held around the full moon in May, that marks the birth, enlightenment and death of the Buddha. Many Buddhists visit temples, make offerings and act generously.
Pilgrimage
a journey to a place linked to the Buddha's life, such as Lumbini, where he was born, or Bodh Gaya, where he gained enlightenment. Pilgrims reflect on his teachings at the site.
draft.remember: Buddhist practices turn beliefs, such as impermanence and respect for the Buddha's teachings, into things people do.

a.q: A Buddhist lays flowers before a Buddha image at a temple and later notes that they have wilted. Which belief does this practice express?
opts: All things are impermanent
The Buddha is a creator god
Offerings earn a reward from the Buddha
Only monks can reach enlightenment
a.why: Wilting flowers show that things change and do not last, which is the Buddhist teaching of impermanence. Offerings are a sign of respect, not a payment to the Buddha, so the reward option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what happens to flowers over a few days.

b.q: Priya travels from Sydney to Bodh Gaya and meditates near the tree linked to the Buddha's enlightenment. Why is this best described as a pilgrimage?
opts: It is a journey to a place linked to the Buddha's life
It is a festival marking the Buddha's birth and death
It is an offering made before a Buddha image in a temple
It is a holiday that replaces regular temple practice
b.why: A pilgrimage is a journey to a site linked to the Buddha, and Bodh Gaya is where he gained enlightenment. Wesak is a festival and puja is an act of offering, so neither describes a journey to a place.
b.clue: Focus on travel to a place, not on a date or an offering.

b.best: It is a journey to a place linked to the Buddha's life

proposal.title: A significant Buddhist practice
card: A Buddhist practice is something Buddhists do that puts their beliefs into action. Doing it shows and strengthens what they hold to be true.
Temple puja
bowing, chanting and offering flowers, candles or incense before an image of the Buddha. It shows respect for the Buddha as a teacher, not as a god who grants wishes.
Wesak
a festival on the full moon of the month of Vesakha, usually in May. Many Buddhists recall the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, make offerings and act generously.
Pilgrimage
a journey to a place linked to the Buddha's life, such as Lumbini, where he was born, or Bodh Gaya, where he gained enlightenment. Being at the site helps pilgrims reflect on his path and their own.
proposal.remember: Each practice turns belief into action: respect at puja, remembering at Wesak, reflection on pilgrimage.

a.q: During puja at a temple in Parramatta, Tom bows three times before an image of the Buddha. What does this act express?
opts: Respect for the Buddha as a teacher of the path
Worship of the Buddha as a god who created the world
A payment to the Buddha in return for good fortune
A way of marking the date of the Buddha's birth
a.why: Bowing in puja shows respect for the Buddha as a teacher whose path Buddhists follow. Buddhists do not see him as a god who grants wishes, so bowing is not a payment for good fortune. Marking his birth belongs to Wesak, not to everyday puja.
a.clue: Think about how Buddhists see the Buddha's role.

b.q: Priya, a Buddhist from Sydney, travels to Bodh Gaya and meditates near the tree linked to the Buddha. Why does this site matter for her pilgrimage?
opts: It links her to where the Buddha gained enlightenment
It links her to the place where the Buddha was born
It honours the Buddha as a god who lives at the site
It earns her good fortune that the Buddha grants
b.why: Bodh Gaya is where the Buddha gained enlightenment, so being there helps Priya reflect on his path and her own. The birthplace option is tempting, but that is Lumbini, not Bodh Gaya. Buddhists do not see the Buddha as a god who lives at a site or grants fortune.
b.clue: Each site matters because of a different event in the Buddha's life.

a.best: Respect for the Buddha as a teacher of the path
